column1: # AnyBook G14 (GA403WR) module plan, ANAL-198. Source of truth for the g14/*.modules.* lists;
# scripts/kernel-g14-modlists.py regenerates them and checks them against a dist.
# Row order is the vendor_dlkm load order. Columns:
#   module      file name in the dist (GKI modules are marked gki in `source`)
#   source      anybook = vendor module from //devices/anybook, gki = //common system_dlkm module
#   bare_metal  first_stage (vendor_boot ramdisk) | load (vendor_dlkm modules.load) | block (in the image, blocklisted)
#   ga403wr     the GA403WR device it drives (evidence/2026-10-16-ga403wr-inventory), or - if none

column6: VM: virtio PCI transport, so a guest can boot from virtio-blk
VM: dep of virtio-gpu. Never present on the laptop
VM: display, so SurfaceFlinger has card0 early as in ANAL-172. Never present on the laptop
VM: keyboard/tablet. Never present on the laptop
/dev/dma_heap/system; Codec2's software codecs and other buffer users allocate from it, and without it media decoding fails (ANAL-176). Googlebook loads it from vendor_dlkm too
efivarfs, so the installer can write firmware boot entries (ANAL-191/192). Loading only registers the filesystem; nothing mounts it by default
ACPI WMI bus; asus-wmi, video and nvidia-wmi-ec-backlight sit on it
exposes the firmware's WMI MOF to userspace; harmless
acpi_video: backlight type selection and brightness hotkeys; amdgpu links it
ACPI platform_profile class used by asus-wmi
hwmon class; amdgpu, k10temp, asus-wmi and mt792x register into it
fan device if the DSDT exposes PNP0C0B; harmless otherwise
thermal zones for the thermal HAL
SMBus host; SPD and EC side channels
creates the two CS35L56 I2C clients from one ACPI node
s2idle entry/exit and the S0i3 counters; needed before the first suspend, not for boot
I2C controllers that carry the touchpad and the amps; second stage is early enough for input
I2C HID ACPI glue. Not first stage: nothing before Android's input stack reads the touchpad
AMD sensor fusion hub; no SFH PCI function on the GA403WR, other Ryzen laptops have one
hotkeys, fan profiles, dgpu_disable, gpu_mux_mode, ppt_* limits
ASUS notebook quirks and keymap. VM: blocked, init returns -ENODEV without the ASUS WMI GUID
hotkeys and keyboard backlight. The keys already work through built-in usbhid/hid-generic, so not first stage
the GA403WR loads it under Linux; acpi_video picks it on MUX laptops when the EC owns brightness

display and GPU. Second stage, see docs/kernel.md: SurfaceFlinger starts after vendor_dlkm loads anyway, the firmware lives in /vendor/firmware, and Googlebook keeps its GPU driver out of first stage too
the GA403WR codec; carries the backported quirk (patch 0002)
other Realtek codecs; same menu as Google's Intel build
other HDMI codecs; dep of nvhdmi-mcp
HDA controller driver. Loaded after the codec drivers: Android disables request_module, so a codec without its driver at probe time falls back to the generic parser
picks ps, SOF or legacy ACP per machine
expected ACP driver on the G14 (no acp-config quirk)
generic ACP; for machines acp-config routes away from snd_pci_ps
Chromebook codec pulled in by the ACP machine drivers; binds only on ACPI/DT match
SOF; for machines acp-config routes to SOF. Needs sof-bin firmware, not shipped
wireless config; vendor module as in Google's Intel build
Realtek Wi-Fi 6/6E/7 in other AMD laptops
btusb links it; Realtek BT in other laptops
dep of nouveau: GPU virtual-address space helpers (ANAL-239)

NVIDIA dGPU, for runtime power management only (ANAL-239): headless, runpm=1 (modules.options), GSP-RM firmware from /vendor/firmware. Last, so amdgpu keeps card0 and renderD128 and every earlier module loads as before. External module (devices/anybook/nvidia)
